label: rejected

evidence.V1: Front outline is a crisp symmetric brilliant (flat girdle line, centred culet), the 3/4 silhouette reads instantly as a gem and the top view is a clean octagon with a table, so it is readable from every angle; A15 X/Y error 0.0.
evidence.V2: Big crown vs pavilion and medium crown/pavilion facets plus girdle band read clearly, but the small tier is only a thin table chamfer ring (visible mainly in the top view) and a few lower-girdle slivers, so the small level barely registers at pickup size.
evidence.V3: Chunky stylised proportions (wide table, short crown, deep pavilion to a centred culet) suit a simulator pickup; no stiff-primitive look, and the 0.95 x 0.68 x 0.9 stud box is sensible.
evidence.V4: Table edge carries a thin chamfer ring and the girdle is a soft band, but the crown and pavilion facet ridges are razor-sharp with no light-catching bevel, so edge treatment is inconsistent (crisp facets acceptable by design, but chamfer width well under the kit's ~0.045 studs).
evidence.V5: Close-ups (crown/pavilion, studio and flat) show flat, evenly lit facets with no pinches, seams or z-fighting; only a soft gradient on the front crown facet and a narrow pale strip on the pavilion's right outline, both reading as facet geometry rather than defects; A17/A18 pass with 0 flips/overlaps.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light crown/table, mid crown sides, dark pavilion) with strong value contrast; crimson and royal colourways keep the same disciplined value ramp.
evidence.V7: 112 tris vs tiny-class target 150 (ceiling 300): at or under target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours and a single-hue 3-value ramp match the kit, but the near-razor edges and thin chamfers differ from the kit's soft ~0.045-stud bevels seen on the Badge_Shield anchor.
evidence.V9: Studio line: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, CollisionFidelity Box, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin centre: correct for a pickup.

evidence.V1: Reads instantly as a cut gem from every angle: front outline is a symmetric crown-over-point diamond, three-quarter silhouette is a rounded crown tapering to a single culet, top view is a clean octagon with inset table; A15 X/Y symmetry error 0.0.
evidence.V2: Big (light crown vs dark pavilion split by a girdle band) and medium (table + 8 crown facets, two-tier pavilion) are clear, but the small level is only the thin table-rim chamfer; in the three-quarter the pavilion reads as one large near-black facet mass with little secondary detail.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised proportion: wide table, slightly domed two-break crown, girdle band thick enough to read, pavilion short enough to stay chunky (0.95 x 0.68 x 0.90 studs); centred and no floating parts.
evidence.V4: Inconsistent: a chamfer catches light around the table rim (visible strip in top view and crown close-up) and the girdle band has defined edges, but crown ridges, pavilion ridges and the culet are razor-crisp with no bevel, so only one edge loop carries a highlight.
evidence.V5: No pinches, seams, z-fighting or cap overlaps in the crown/pavilion studio and flat close-ups (A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces); facets are crisp by design. Only a mild soft gradient across the front crown facet in the front view, within kit smooth-shading norms.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one hue (teal) in three values (light crown/table, mid girdle, dark pavilion); colourways crimson and royal keep the same value structure cleanly.
evidence.V7: 112 tris vs tiny-class target 150 (ceiling 300): under target with no wasted loops.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, single hue in 3 values, chamfered table rim and smooth shading match the kit; stylised low-poly look sits alongside the Badge_Shield anchor.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, CollisionFidelity Box, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

evidence.V1: Front reads as the classic gem icon (girdle x=102..410 around apex x=256, A15 X/Y 0.0); top shows a clear octagon with table; 3/4 silhouette is a recognisable gem from every view, though the crown outline is somewhat rounded.
evidence.V2: Big crown/pavilion split and a medium girdle band plus crown facets are clear, but the only small detail is a thin table-edge chamfer that disappears at play size, and the pavilion is a plain cone of large triangles.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised brilliant: a squat, wide crown over a deep pointed pavilion, centred and symmetric with nothing floating; the proportions suit a chunky pickup.
evidence.V4: The table rim has a narrow chamfer that catches light (top view ring, crown close-up), but the girdle-to-crown and girdle-to-pavilion edges and the crown facet ridges are razor-sharp, so bevel treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (studio and flat) show crisp planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray triangles; the gradients on the crown faces are specular, not normal smear; A17/A18 are clean (0 self-intersections, 0 cap overlaps, 0 flipped faces).
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light crown, mid girdle, dark pavilion), with strong value contrast; the crimson and royal colourways keep the same disciplined three-value split.
evidence.V7: 112 tris against a tiny-class target of 150 and a ceiling of 300.
evidence.V8: One white material with vertex colours and a single-hue palette match the kit, but most edges lack the kit's ~0.045 stud chamfer; it looks sharper and harder than the soft-bevelled kit pieces.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, CollisionFidelity Box, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin at centre.

artifacts: Narrow pale sliver strip along the pavilion's right outline in the 3/4 and pavilion close-up (likely an edge-on facet, minor)
Soft gradient band across the front crown facet in the front view (smoothing bleed on a flat facet, minor)
Mild soft shading gradient across the front crown facet in the front view (not a visible defect at gameplay size)
none blocking; minor: the table chamfer strip is so thin it reads as a dark line in the flat close-up rather than a lit bevel
top_fixes: Add a consistent small chamfer (~0.03-0.045 studs) to the girdle edges and the main crown/pavilion facet ridges so edges catch light like the rest of the kit
Strengthen the small detail tier: widen the table bevel or add star/upper-girdle facets so the crown reads with a clear small level at pickup size
Clean up the thin sliver facets at the pavilion outline/lower girdle so each pavilion facet reads as one clear plane
Add a small consistent chamfer (~0.03-0.045 studs) to crown and pavilion ridges and blunt the culet so every facet edge catches a highlight, not only the table rim
Break up the dark pavilion mass with a small-scale tier (lower-girdle or star facets) or lift its darkest value slightly so the small level of the hierarchy reads at 64 px
Optionally add star facets around the table to give the crown a small-detail ring
Add a consistent small chamfer (~0.03-0.045 studs) to the girdle top and bottom edges and the crown facet ridges so the edges catch light like the rest of the kit
Widen the table-edge chamfer so it reads as a lit rim at play size, giving the gem a visible small-scale detail tier
Sharpen the crown silhouette (slightly flatter, more angular crown facets) so the 3/4 outline reads less like a rounded dome
